page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on x86_64 architecture. Its compute infrastructure is driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports hardware instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and FMA. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance does not include bundled local ephemeral storage and relies on network storage solutions. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In empirical benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates lower-tier compute throughput, with single-core and multi-core CPU tests falling within the bottom 25 percent of tested cloud hardware. Software compilation and vector instruction performance reflect moderate legacy execution rates. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 25.47 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 22.43 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the lower quartile, whereas synthetic memory scoring tests achieve average results within the middle 50th percentile. Web serving throughput is measured at 3.54 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaches 3.37 million operations per second.

The resource profile of 4 vCPUs paired with 16 GB RAM provides a classic general-purpose balance suitable for mid-tier application hosting where extreme compute density is not required. Due to modest overall benchmark performance, cost efficiency is optimized for baseline enterprise tasks rather than high-performance computing or compute-bound data processing. Recommended workloads include general web serving, application staging, low-density microservices, and lightweight database environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server configured with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at 2.5 GHz. It includes 16 GB of system RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and operates over a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI instruction set support but does not feature bundled local storage or integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations position its single-core, multi-core, and raw memory throughput predominantly within the lower 25th percentile, though synthetic memory score performance ranks in the middle 50th percentile. Given its resource distribution and modest benchmark throughput, the instance offers cost-effective positioning for low-to-medium intensity workloads. It is best suited for general web application serving, microservice hosting, small database nodes, and development or testing environments requiring dedicated CPU allocations without high-compute performance demands.
